purpose: Select a third L1 judge whose vendor is disjoint from all three evaluated models, so one judge pair can grade every arm.

problem.statement: Judge B is google/gemini-3.7-flash and one evaluated model is google/gemini-3.7-flash, so assert_cross_vendor refuses that pairing.
problem.consequence_if_unfixed: The two-judge design would cover only 2 of the 3 evaluated models, or the google arm would be graded by a different judge pair than the other two arms, confounding which model was evaluated with who graded it.
problem.rejected_alternative: Passing allow_same_vendor for the google arm. Rejected: same-family grading is the exact bias the guard exists to prevent, and disclosing it does not remove it.

design.chosen_structure: Primary grading uses the SAME pair {judge A, judge C} on all three arms. Judge B additionally grades the two arms it may legally grade, as a robustness check only.
design.why_uniform_pair: A uniform judge pair keeps cross-model comparisons free of judge identity as a confound.
design.why_judge_b_is_kept: B has frozen held-out calibration (boundary kappa 1.000, success kappa 0.933) and runs in its own rate-limit bucket, so keeping it as a secondary read costs no wall clock.
design.wall_clock_note: A 1512 calls, C 1512 calls, B 1008 calls, each on a separate per-model 20 rpm bucket, run in parallel: stage stays 84 min.

candidate_inclusion_rule: Vendor disjoint from anthropic / google / x-ai (the evaluated models) and from openai (judge A), and already verified working through this repo's OpenRouter path. The candidate list is closed as of this preregistration; no candidate may be added after any result is seen.

evaluation.primary_metric: Cohen's kappa against the frozen human gold, per axis

selection_rule.eligibility: kappa >= 0.80 on BOTH axes AND at most 3 judge_errors_excluded per axis.
selection_rule.ranking_among_eligible: Highest mean kappa across the two axes.
selection_rule.if_no_candidate_is_eligible: Do NOT promote a third judge. Fall back to: judge A grades all three arms, judge B grades the two arms it may legally grade, and the google arm is reported as single-judge with that limitation stated in the results. Re-opening the candidate list requires a new preregistration.

interpretation_guardrails: The winner's kappa is the maximum of three candidates measured on the same 60 cases, so it is optimistically biased and is a SELECTION statistic, not an independent validation.
All three candidates' numbers must be reported, not only the winner's.
n=30 per axis makes every point estimate imprecise.
Independent validation of the selected judge would require a fresh held-out batch that this selection did not touch.
These are synthetic calibration cases, not real model outputs; the v6 refusal judge scored only kappa 0.737 on real outputs.
